newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chechens at Swiss forum want single Caucasus mkt.
newsitem.headline: Chechens at Swiss forum want single Caucasus mkt.

text.p: Rebels turned businessmen from Chechnya announced plans for a common Caucasus economic market at a Swiss international business forum on Friday and appealed for Western investment.

Teamed up with globe-trotting Saudi business tycoon Adnan Khashoggi who announced plans to set up a joint investment bank for the Caucasus, they appealed to investors to fund oil, telecoms and transport projects in the volatile region.
The mountainous region has been ridden by ethnic strife, banditry and wars since 1991's break-up of the Soviet Union, and Chechnya was ruined by a war between rebels and Russian troops.
But Chechnya's efforts to rebuild its economy were reflected vividly by the presence of its business delegation at the forum in the Swiss mountain resort of Crans Montana.

Khoz-Akhmed Noukhayev, president of the newly-formed U.S.-Caucasus International Chamber of Commerce, said he was firing at Russian tanks in Chechnya's capital Grozny more than two years ago during the breakaway region's bloody war.
Now, it's time for peace and business, said Noukhayev, dressed in a smart suit and accompanied by an aide wearing the traditional woolly Chechen hat.
"We believe the path to peace in our region lies through economic integration," Noukhayev told the annual forum at the Swiss mountain resort of Crans Montana.
"We hope to attract foreign investment by harmonising our taxes and legislation. We believe the Caucasus open market is a real opportunity for international companies and investors."
Moscow withdrew its last troops from Chechya early this year after failing to crush the separatists over 21 months of war but remains implacably opposed to their demands for independence.
Noukhayev said Chechen businessmen wanted to cooperate with Russia: "Russia is our neighbour. We need to live together peacefully. We need to become business partners," he said.
He said the common market modelled on the European Union would include Azerbaijan, Georgia, Chechnya and south Russia.
"Our region is rich in oil, natural gas, minerals and agricultural resources. Opportunities await investors," he said.

"Many experts think the Caucasus will become a new Gulf in terms of prosperity. We want to develop ourselves in the middle of a Silk Road from Shangh to Paris and from Astrakhan to Beirut. We want to play a key role in transport and communications between Europe and Asia."
The Chechen initiative won the blessing of an unlikely partner, the Paris-based Saudi businessman Khashoggi.
He told reporters at the forum that he planned to set up a joint investment bank to finance projects in the Caucasus. It would have a $100 million capital and be operational next year.
"This region is an opportunity for us. We are establishing business links with Chechnya and Georgia, with Russia's blessing of course," Khashoggi said.

The region stretching from Azerbaijan to western Kazakhstan has vast oil and gas reserves. The whiff of oil has attracted the attention of United States, Russia, Turkey and Iran amidst intense pipeline politics.
